evals.prompt: Write a README for my new CLI tool aimed at first-time users.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not start drafting content immediately; first asks clarifying questions about audience, purpose, scope, and constraints, and confirms whether this is a new document or a revision before moving into Stage 2 structuring.
assertions: Does not produce README body content before gathering audience, purpose, and scope
Confirms whether this is a new document or a revision of existing work
Sequences the response as context gathering (Stage 1) before structure or drafting (Stage 2)

evals.prompt: Write a README for internal-tool-x aimed at platform engineers who need to get it running locally within 10 minutes. Keep it under 400 words and match the style of our other tool READMEs in docs/tools/. Here are my rough notes: [notes attached].
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes that audience, purpose, length, and style constraints were already supplied and does not re-ask for them; only asks about genuinely missing inputs such as who can provide reader validation, then moves toward Stage 2 structuring.
assertions: Does not re-ask for audience, purpose, or length constraints already stated in the prompt
Only requests genuinely missing information, such as a reader for validation
Moves toward drafting structure without restating information the user already gave

evals.prompt: Refactor our on-call runbook so it's organized by task instead of by system, and get an on-call engineer to test it before we call it done.
evals.expected_behavior: Produces a runbook reorganized around operator tasks, incorporates feedback from a real reader outside the original authoring team, and delivers a finalized document plus a summary of what changed based on that feedback.
assertions: Final document is organized by task rather than by system, matching the stated goal
Incorporates feedback from at least one reader outside the original authoring team, such as an on-call engineer
Delivers a finalized document plus a summary of what changed based on reader feedback
Does not treat copyediting or polish as complete before structure and reader validation are settled

evals.prompt: Our integration guide needs to serve both external customers and our internal support team at once — write it up.
evals.expected_behavior: Flags during context gathering that serving both audiences in one document risks being unfocused, and recommends either splitting into audience-specific documents or clearly scoping which audience the document primarily serves, per the skill's guardrail.
assertions: Identifies that covering both external customers and internal support in one document risks satisfying neither
Recommends splitting into separate audience-scoped documents or explicitly narrowing scope to one primary audience
Raises this tension during context gathering rather than after a full draft already exists

evals.prompt: Can you fix this typo in the README where it says 'recieve' instead of 'receive'?
evals.expected_behavior: Makes the direct one-off fix without invoking the three-stage co-authoring workflow, per the skill's own 'Do not use this skill when' guidance for minor style or typo fixes.
assertions: Makes the fix directly without asking about audience, purpose, or scope
Does not invoke Stage 1 context gathering for a single typo fix
Does not propose a reader-feedback or validation plan for a trivial correction

evals.prompt: Run a readability audit on this doc and give me a Flesch Reading Ease score.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes this is a solo prose-quality audit rather than structured co-authoring, and routes to writing-and-editing's readability-audit mode instead of running the three-stage workflow.
assertions: Does not initiate Stage 1 context gathering or a reader-testing workflow for an audit-only request
Identifies writing-and-editing (readability-audit mode) as the appropriate skill for this request
Does not draft new document content in response to an audit request
